q: What native runtime is Open Container Initiative (OCI) compliant?
e: runC is the OCI-compliant reference container runtime.

q: Which API object is the recommended way to run a scalable, stateless application on your cluster?
e: Deployments manage ReplicaSets and provide declarative updates, making them the recommended way to run scalable, stateless apps.

q: A CronJob is scheduled to run every one hour. What happens in the cluster when it's time for it to run?
o: Kubelet watches API Server for CronJob objects and runs the Pod directly.
Kube-scheduler watches API Server for CronJob objects.
CronJob controller creates a Pod and waits until it finishes.
CronJob controller creates a Job, then the Job controller creates a Pod and waits until it finishes.
e: The CronJob controller creates a Job on schedule, and the Job controller then creates the Pod(s).

q: What is the purpose of the kubelet component within a Kubernetes cluster?
o: A dashboard for managing and troubleshooting applications.
A network proxy implementing part of the Service concept.
A component that watches for unscheduled Pods and selects a node.
An agent on each node that ensures containers are running in a Pod.
e: The kubelet is the node agent ensuring containers described in Pod specs are actually running.

q: What is the default value for --authorization-mode in the Kubernetes API server?
e: The historical/raw default is AlwaysAllow, though most distributions explicitly enable RBAC.

q: An org needs to run 1000 batch jobs of 1 hour each every Monday, cost-effectively. What's best?
o: Run a fixed group of nodes reserved via taints/tolerations/nodeSelectors.
Leverage the Cluster Autoscaler to start/stop nodes as needed.
Commit to reserved instances for discounted pricing.
Use PriorityClasses so the batch job gets priority.
e: The Cluster Autoscaler scales nodes up only when needed and back down after, which is most cost-effective for bursty batch work.

q: What is a Kubernetes service with no cluster IP address called?
e: A Service with clusterIP: None is called a headless Service.

q: CI/CD stands for:
e: CI/CD stands for Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment (or Delivery).

q: What default level of protection is applied to data in Kubernetes Secrets?
e: By default Secret data is only base64 encoded, not encrypted, unless encryption-at-rest is separately configured.

q: What function does kube-proxy provide to a cluster?
o: Forwarding data to the correct endpoints for Services.
Managing data egress from nodes to the network.
Managing access to the Kubernetes API.
e: kube-proxy maintains network rules that forward traffic to the correct Service endpoints.

q: How long should a stable API element be supported (at minimum) after deprecation?
e: Stable (GA) APIs must be supported for at least 12 months (or 3 releases) after deprecation.

q: What is the name of the lightweight Kubernetes distribution built for IoT and edge computing?
e: k3s is a certified, lightweight Kubernetes distribution designed for edge and IoT.

q: Kubernetes ___ automatically manages the number of nodes in your cluster to meet demand.
e: The Cluster Autoscaler adjusts node count based on scheduling demand.

q: Which statement is correct concerning Open Policy Agent (OPA)?
o: Policies must be written in Python.
Kubernetes can use it to validate requests and apply policies.
Policies can only be tested when published.
It cannot be used outside Kubernetes.
e: OPA (via admission webhooks like Gatekeeper) validates and enforces policy on API requests, and works outside Kubernetes too.

q: In a cloud native world, what does IaC stand for?
e: IaC = Infrastructure as Code.

q: In which framework do developers no longer deal with capacity, deployments, scaling, fault tolerance, and OS?
e: Serverless computing abstracts away infrastructure concerns like capacity and scaling.

q: Which characteristic is associated with container orchestration?
e: Dynamic scheduling of containers onto hosts is a core orchestration characteristic.

q: Which workload requires a headless service while deploying into the namespace?
e: StatefulSets use a headless Service to provide stable per-Pod network identities.

q: What is Helm?
o: An open source dashboard for Kubernetes.
A package manager for Kubernetes applications.
e: Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes, using charts to define, install, and upgrade applications.

q: Which is the correct kubectl command to display logs in real time?
e: The -f (follow) flag streams logs in real time.

q: How can you load and generate data required before Pod startup?
o: Use an init container with shared file storage.
Use a sidecar container with shared volume.
Use another pod with a PVC.
e: Init containers run to completion before app containers start and can prep shared data via a shared volume.

q: What is the core functionality of GitOps tools like Argo CD and Flux?
o: They track human production changes and generate an audit trail.
They replace human operations with a Git-command agent.
They automatically create PRs when dependencies are outdated.
They continuously compare desired state in Git with actual state and act on differences.
e: GitOps tools continuously reconcile the live cluster to match the declared state in Git.

q: Which resource workload ensures that all (or some) nodes run a copy of a Pod?
e: A DaemonSet ensures a copy of a Pod runs on all or a selected subset of nodes.

q: What does CRD stand for, used to extend the Kubernetes API?
e: CRD = Custom Resource Definition, used with the aggregation layer to extend the API.

q: The Kubernetes project's work is carried primarily by SIGs. What does SIG stand for?
e: SIG = Special Interest Group.

q: What is the order of the 4C's in Cloud Native Security, starting with the layer a user has most control over?
e: The 4Cs go Code, Container, Cluster, Cloud, from most to least user control.

q: Which group of container runtimes provides additional sandboxed isolation and elevated security?
e: gVisor (runsc) and Kata Containers add sandboxing beyond standard runtimes.

q: What is the common standard for Service Meshes?
e: SMI (Service Mesh Interface) was the common standard interface for service meshes.

q: Which statement about Ingress is correct?
o: Ingress tracks network endpoints within a cluster.
Ingress is a Service type like NodePort and ClusterIP.
Ingress specifies how a Pod is allowed to communicate.
Ingress exposes routes from outside the cluster to services in the cluster.
e: Ingress exposes HTTP/HTTPS routes from outside the cluster to internal Services.

q: What best describes cloud native service discovery?
o: A mechanism for applications/microservices to locate each other on a network.
A procedure for discovering a MAC address for an IP.
Automatically assigning IP addresses to devices.
A protocol turning domain names into IP addresses.
e: Service discovery lets services locate each other dynamically on the network.

q: What components are common in a service mesh?
e: A service mesh consists of a data-plane of proxies and a control plane managing them.

q: Which storage operator in Kubernetes can help the system self-scale, self-heal, etc.?
e: Rook is a storage orchestrator that automates self-managing, self-scaling, self-healing storage services.

q: What fields must exist in any Kubernetes object (e.g., YAML) file?
e: apiVersion, kind, and metadata are required top-level fields (along with spec, in most cases).

q: Which of the following would fall under the responsibilities of an SRE?
o: Creating a monitoring baseline for an application.
Submitting a budget for running an app in the cloud.
Writing policy on how to submit a code change.
e: SREs focus on reliability practices like establishing monitoring baselines.

q: What are the initial namespaces that Kubernetes starts with?
e: A fresh cluster starts with default, kube-system, kube-public, and kube-node-lease.

q: What is a probe within Kubernetes?
o: A monitoring mechanism of the Kubernetes API.
A pre-operational scope issued by kubectl.
A diagnostic performed periodically by the kubelet on a container.
A logging mechanism of the Kubernetes API.
e: Probes are periodic diagnostics (liveness/readiness/startup) run by the kubelet against containers.

q: Which Kubernetes feature guards against split-brain scenarios with distributed applications?
e: StatefulSets provide stable identity and ordered operations that help avoid split-brain in distributed apps.
note: Community vote is split (57% StatefulSet / 43% consensus protocols) — treat with care.

q: What feature must a CNI support to control specific traffic flows for workloads?
e: CNI plugins that support NetworkPolicy allow controlling ingress/egress traffic flows.

q: What is the main role of Kubernetes DNS within a cluster?
o: Acts as a DNS server for VMs outside the cluster.
Provides DNS as a Service for user-owned domains.
Converts IPv6 calls to IPv4 for dual-stack Pods.
Provides consistent DNS names for Pods and Services that need to communicate.
e: Cluster DNS (CoreDNS) gives stable, resolvable names to Pods and Services.

q: A Service of type LoadBalancer has external-ip stuck 'Pending'. Which component is failing?
e: The Cloud Controller Manager provisions the cloud load balancer; if it fails, external-ip stays Pending.

q: What are the characteristics for building every cloud-native application?
e: The commonly cited cloud native characteristics are Resiliency, Agility, Operability, and Observability.

q: What does CNCF stand for?
e: CNCF = Cloud Native Computing Foundation.

q: Kubernetes supports multiple virtual clusters backed by the same physical cluster. These are called:
e: Namespaces provide virtual cluster partitioning within one physical cluster.

q: What component enables end users, cluster parts, and external components to communicate with one another?
e: The Kubernetes API is the central communication interface for the whole system.

q: Which command lists the resource types that exist within a cluster?
e: kubectl api-resources lists all resource types available in the cluster.

q: Which of these components is part of the Kubernetes Control Plane?
e: cloud-controller-manager is a control-plane component; kube-proxy and kubelet run on nodes.

q: Which system is NOT compatible with the CRI runtime interface standard?
e: systemd is an init system, not a container runtime implementing CRI.

q: What is a key feature of a container network?
o: Proxying REST requests across a set of containers.
Allowing containers on separate hosts to communicate.
Allowing containers on the same host to communicate.
e: A container network's key feature is enabling cross-host container communication.

q: How can you monitor the progress of an updated Deployment/DaemonSet/StatefulSet?
e: kubectl rollout status reports live rollout progress.

q: What is the goal of load balancing?
o: Automatically measure request performance across instances.
Automatically distribute requests across different app versions.
Automatically distribute app instances across the cluster.
Automatically distribute requests across instances of an application.
e: Load balancing spreads incoming requests evenly across available application instances.

q: How are ReplicaSets and Deployments related?
o: Deployments manage ReplicaSets and provide declarative updates to Pods.
ReplicaSets manage stateful apps, Deployments manage stateless apps.
Deployments are runtime instances of ReplicaSets.
ReplicaSets are subsets of Jobs/CronJobs using imperative Deployments.
e: A Deployment is a higher-level controller that manages one or more ReplicaSets to enable declarative rollouts.

q: What factors influence the Kubernetes scheduler when placing Pods on nodes?
o: Pod memory requests, node taints, and Pod affinity.
Pod labels, node labels, and request labels.
Node taints, node level, and Pod priority.
Pod priority, container command, and node labels.
e: The scheduler weighs resource requests, taints/tolerations, and affinity/anti-affinity rules, among others.

q: What is the core metric type in Prometheus used to represent a single value that can go up and down?
e: A Gauge represents a value that can arbitrarily increase or decrease.

q: What is the primary mechanism to identify grouped objects in a Kubernetes cluster?
e: Labels are the key/value metadata used to identify and group objects.
note: Community vote is close (52% Labels / 48% Label Selector).

q: What is the name of the Kubernetes resource used to expose an application?
e: A Service is the resource used to expose a set of Pods as a network endpoint.

q: What is a DaemonSet?
o: A workload that ensures a specific set of nodes run a copy of a Pod.
A workload maintaining a stable set of replica Pods on any node.
A workload that runs periodically on a schedule.
A workload providing ordering, uniqueness, and identity guarantees.
e: A DaemonSet ensures a Pod copy runs on all (or a selected subset of) nodes.

q: What telemetry component represents a series of related distributed events encoding an end-to-end request flow?
e: Traces represent the end-to-end path of a request across a distributed system (composed of spans).

q: In the Kubernetes platform, which component is responsible for running containers?
e: CRI-O is a container runtime that actually runs containers via the CRI interface.

q: Services and Pods in Kubernetes are ______ objects.
e: Kubernetes API objects, including Services and Pods, are managed as REST resources.

q: What Kubernetes component handles network communications inside/outside the cluster using OS packet filtering if available?
e: kube-proxy implements Service networking using iptables/IPVS or similar OS-level packet filtering.

q: What control plane component exposes the programmatic interface to create, manage, and interact with objects?
e: The kube-apiserver is the front-end API for the whole control plane.

q: Which type of Service requires manual creation of Endpoints?
e: Selector-less Services need their Endpoints/EndpointSlices created manually.

q: Which command retrieves documentation and field definitions for a Kubernetes resource?
e: kubectl explain shows field-level docs for a resource type.

q: Which lightweight tool manages traffic flows, enforces access policies, and aggregates telemetry without app code changes?
e: Linkerd is a lightweight service mesh providing traffic management, policy, and telemetry transparently.

q: Which Kubernetes resource uses the immutable: true boolean field?
e: ConfigMaps (and Secrets) support an immutable field to prevent further updates.

q: Which statement about the Kubernetes network model is correct?
o: Pods can only communicate via a Service.
Pods can communicate with all Pods without NAT.
The Pod IP is only visible inside a Pod.
The Service IP is used for Service-to-Service communication.
e: The flat Kubernetes network model requires that all Pods can reach all other Pods without NAT.

q: What is the resource type used to package sets of containers for scheduling in a cluster?
e: A Pod packages one or more containers as the schedulable unit.

q: Can a Kubernetes Service expose multiple ports?
o: No, only one port per Service.
Yes, but each port must have an unambiguous name.
Yes, the only requirement is different port numbers.
No, only port 443 can be exposed.
e: A multi-port Service requires each port to be named uniquely.
note: Community vote is close (56%/44%) on the exact wording of the requirement.

q: Which persona is normally responsible for defining, testing, and running an incident management process?
e: SREs typically own incident management processes.

q: What is the default deployment strategy in Kubernetes?
e: RollingUpdate is the default Deployment strategy.

q: Which command provides info about the replicas field within a deployment's spec?
e: kubectl explain can target a nested field path like deployment.spec.replicas.

q: Which is a responsibility of the governance board of an open source project?
o: Review pull requests in the main branch.
Define the license used in the project.
e: Governance boards typically define how the project's community operates ('terms of engagement').

q: What is the role of a NetworkPolicy in Kubernetes?
o: Classify the Pods as isolated and non-isolated.
Prevent loopback or incoming host traffic.
e: NetworkPolicies determine which Pods are isolated (traffic-restricted) vs. non-isolated.

q: What are the most important resources to guarantee etcd cluster performance?
e: etcd is latency-sensitive; fast disk I/O and network throughput are critical.

q: How do you deploy a workload to Kubernetes without additional tools?
o: Create a Bash script and run it on a worker node.
Create a Helm Chart and install it with helm.
Create a manifest and apply it with kubectl.
Create a Python script and run it with kubectl.
e: kubectl apply -f against a plain manifest requires no additional tooling.

q: How do you run a command in a running container of a Pod?
e: kubectl exec <pod> -- <cmd> runs a command inside a running container.

q: How do you create a headless service?
e: Setting clusterIP: None creates a headless Service.

q: How does dynamic storage provisioning work?
o: A user requests storage by including an existing storage class in their PVC.
An admin creates a storage class and includes it in the pod YAML, skipping the PVC.
A pod requests storage by including a storage class and pod name in a PVC.
An admin creates a PV and includes its name in the pod YAML.
e: Dynamic provisioning: a PVC references a StorageClass, which auto-provisions a matching PV.

q: Which tasks are performed by a container orchestration tool?
o: Schedule, scale, and manage the health of containers.
Create images, scale, and manage the health of containers.
Debug applications, and manage the health of containers.
Store images, scale, and manage the health of containers.
e: Orchestrators schedule, scale, and manage container health — not image building or storage.

q: Which is a definition of Hybrid Cloud?
o: Combining public/private data centers from the same provider only.
Combining public clouds, excluding different availability zones.
Combining services across different public and private clouds, including on-prem.
Combining public/private data centers, excluding serverless functions.
e: Hybrid cloud spans multiple public/private clouds and on-premises data centers.

q: What is a Kubernetes Service Endpoint?
o: The API Endpoint of the cluster.
A special Pod name in kube-system.
An IP address reachable from the Internet.
An object holding the IP addresses of individual Pods assigned to it.
e: An Endpoints/EndpointSlice object tracks the actual Pod IPs backing a Service.

q: Why is Cloud-Native Architecture important?
o: It revolves around containers, microservices and pipelines.
It removes constraints to rapid innovation.
It's a modern approach to deployment and pipelines.
It's a bleeding-edge technology and service.
e: Cloud native architecture matters because it removes constraints that slow down innovation.

q: Which Kubernetes component is the smallest deployable unit of computing?
e: The Pod is the smallest deployable unit managed directly by Kubernetes.

q: What kubectl command retrieves CPU and memory resource consumption for nodes or Pods?
e: kubectl top shows live resource usage for nodes or Pods (via metrics-server).

q: Which are the two primary modes for Service discovery within a Kubernetes cluster?
e: Kubernetes supports Service discovery via injected environment variables and cluster DNS.

q: Which capability are you allowed to add to a container using the Restricted Pod Security Standard?
e: The Restricted profile only permits adding back NET_BIND_SERVICE among capabilities.

q: What methods can you use to scale a deployment?
o: kubectl scale deployment and kubectl edit deployment.
e: Both kubectl scale and kubectl edit (changing replicas) can scale a Deployment.

q: What is a sidecar container?
o: A Pod that runs next to another container within the same Pod.
A container that runs next to another Pod within the same namespace.
A container that runs next to another container within the same Pod.
A Pod that runs next to another Pod within the same namespace.
e: A sidecar is an additional container co-located with the main container inside the same Pod.

q: Which is an industry-standard container runtime with an emphasis on simplicity, robustness, and portability?
e: containerd is the widely-adopted CNCF container runtime known for simplicity and portability.

q: What does vertical scaling an application deployment describe best?
o: Adding/removing node instances to meet demand.
Adding/removing resources to applications to meet demand.
Adding/removing app instances of the same app to meet demand.
e: Vertical scaling changes the resources (CPU/memory) allocated to existing instances.

q: Which Prometheus metric represents a single value that can go up and down?
e: A Gauge can increase or decrease arbitrarily, unlike a Counter which only increases.

q: What is Serverless computing?
o: A computing method providing backend services on an as-used basis.
A method for AI/ML operating systems.
A method for quantum computing operating systems.
A method for cloud computing operating systems.
e: Serverless provides backend compute billed and provisioned on an as-used, event-driven basis.

q: What is the purpose of the CRI?
o: Provide runtime integration control when multiple runtimes are used.
Support container replication and scaling on nodes.
Provide an interface allowing Kubernetes to support pluggable container runtimes.
Allow definition of dynamic resource criteria across containers.
e: The Container Runtime Interface (CRI) lets Kubernetes support pluggable container runtimes.

q: There's a requirement to run a database backup every day. Which resource achieves that?
e: A CronJob runs Jobs on a recurring, time-based schedule — ideal for daily backups.

q: In CNCF, who develops specifications for industry standards around container formats and runtimes?
e: OCI develops the open standards for container image formats and runtimes.

q: Which of the following includes valid API versions?
e: Valid Kubernetes API version strings look like v1alpha1, v2beta3, v2 — following the vX(alpha|beta)Y convention.

q: Which command views a snapshot of previously terminated 'ruby' container logs from Pod web-1?
e: -p (previous) plus -c <container> targets logs from the terminated instance of that specific container.

q: A Kubernetes _____ is an abstraction that defines a logical set of Pods and a policy by which to access them.
e: This is the textbook definition of a Kubernetes Service.

q: How many hosts are required for a highly available cluster using an external etcd topology?
o: Four hosts: two control-plane, two etcd.
Four hosts: one control-plane, three etcd.
Three hosts: control-plane and etcd share hosts.
Six hosts: three control-plane, three etcd.
e: External etcd topology separates the etcd cluster from control-plane nodes, needing 3+3 hosts for HA.

q: Which event will cause the kube-scheduler to assign a Pod to a node?
o: The Pod crashes because of an error.
A new node is added to the cluster.
CPU load on a node becomes too high.
A new Pod is created and has no assigned node.
e: The scheduler acts on Pods that exist but have no nodeName assigned yet.

q: What helps an organization deliver software more securely at a higher velocity?
e: A CI/CD pipeline automates testing and delivery, improving both security and velocity.

q: Which resource do you use to attach a volume in a Pod?
e: A Pod references a PersistentVolumeClaim, which binds to a PersistentVolume, to attach storage.

q: Which key-value store is used to persist Kubernetes cluster data?
e: etcd is the distributed key-value store backing all cluster state.

q: What Linux namespace is shared by default by containers running within a Kubernetes Pod?
e: Containers in the same Pod share the network namespace by default.

q: What is a Dockerfile?
o: A bash script that automatically builds a docker image.
A config file defining which registry to push a container to.
A text file with commands to assemble an image.
An image layer created by a running container.
e: A Dockerfile is a text file listing build instructions used to assemble a container image.

q: What does the nodeSelector within a PodSpec use to place Pods on target nodes?
e: nodeSelector matches Pods to nodes using node labels.

q: What do Deployments and StatefulSets have in common?
o: They manage Pods based on an identical container spec.
They support the OnDelete update strategy.
They support ordered, graceful deployment and scaling.
They maintain a sticky identity for each of their Pods.
e: Both manage a set of Pods created from one common Pod template/spec.

q: What is the practice of bringing financial accountability to the variable spend model of cloud resources?
e: FinOps is the practice/culture of managing and optimizing variable cloud spend.

q: What is a best practice to minimize container image size?
e: Multi-stage builds discard build-time dependencies, shrinking the final image.

q: Which tools enable HPA to use custom, application-generated metrics to trigger scaling?
e: Prometheus plus the prometheus-adapter exposes custom metrics the HPA can consume via the custom metrics API.

q: Which of the following is a valid PromQL query?
e: PromQL uses a metric name with a label-matcher selector in curly braces, not SQL syntax.

q: Which best describes horizontally scaling an application deployment?
o: Adding/removing node instances to the cluster to meet demand.
Adding/removing application instances of the same app to meet demand.
Adding/removing resources to application instances to meet demand.
e: Horizontal scaling changes the number of replica instances of an application.

q: How many different Kubernetes Service types can you define?
e: The four Service types are ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, and ExternalName.

q: What is the difference between a Deployment and a ReplicaSet?
o: With a Deployment you can't control the number of pod replicas.
A ReplicaSet does not guarantee a stable set of replica pods.
A Deployment is basically the same as a ReplicaSet with annotations.
A Deployment is a higher-level concept that manages ReplicaSets.
e: Deployments sit above ReplicaSets, managing them to enable rollouts and rollbacks.

q: The Container Runtime Interface (CRI) defines the protocol for communication between:
o: The kubelet and the container runtime.
The container runtime and the image registry.
e: CRI standardizes kubelet-to-container-runtime communication.

q: Which authorization mode allows granular control over operations different entities can perform on different objects?
e: RBAC provides fine-grained, role-based permission control over API operations.

q: Which is a correct definition of a Helm chart?
o: A collection of YAML files bundled in a tar.gz, applied without decompressing.
A collection of JSON files with all resource definitions.
A collection of YAML files applied via kubectl.
A package-like bundle containing all resource definitions to run an app on Kubernetes.
e: A Helm chart packages templated Kubernetes manifests and metadata needed to run an application.

q: Which statement is true about namespaces in Kubernetes?
o: You can nest a namespace within another namespace.
You can create two resources of the same kind/name in a namespace.
The default namespace exists when a new cluster is created.
All objects in the cluster are namespaced by default.
e: A default namespace is created automatically for every new cluster.

q: How does Horizontal Pod Autoscaling work in Kubernetes?
o: It adds/reduces CPU or memory allocated to pods based on load.
It adds pods above threshold but never reduces them.
It scales DaemonSet pod counts based on load.
It adds pods above threshold and reduces them below threshold.
e: HPA changes the replica count up or down based on observed metrics vs. target thresholds.

q: What is a Pod?
o: A group of one or more containers within Kubernetes.
e: A Pod is a group of one or more co-located, co-scheduled containers.

q: What element allows Kubernetes to run Pods across the fleet of nodes?
e: The kubelet on each node is what actually runs Pods there.

q: What is the Kubernetes object used for running a recurring workload?
e: A CronJob runs a workload on a repeating, time-based schedule.

q: In the DevOps framework and culture, who builds, automates, and offers continuous delivery tools for developer teams?
e: Platform engineers build and maintain the tooling/platform that developer teams use for delivery.

q: Which kubectl command is useful for collecting information about any active resource type in a cluster?
e: kubectl describe gives detailed status/info about any resource instance.

q: The cloud native architecture centered around microservices provides a strong system that ensures ______________.
e: Microservices architectures are prized for the resiliency they can provide.

q: Which is the correct command to run an nginx deployment with 2 replicas?
e: kubectl create deploy --image= --replicas= is the correct imperative syntax.

q: What does 'Continuous Integration' mean?
o: Continuous integration and testing of code from multiple sources manually.
Continuous integration and testing of code from multiple sources via automation.
Continuous integration of changes from one environment to another.
Continuous integration of new tools to support developers.
e: CI automates the integration and testing of code changes from multiple contributors.

q: Which statement is true about considerations for large Kubernetes clusters?
o: Supports up to 1000 nodes, max 1000 containers per node.
Supports up to 5000 nodes, max 500 pods per node.
Supports up to 5000 nodes, max 110 pods per node.
Supports up to 50 nodes, max 1000 containers per node.
e: Kubernetes' documented scalability guidance is up to 5000 nodes and ~110 pods per node.

q: Which component of the node is responsible for running workloads?
e: The container runtime is what actually executes containers, invoked by the kubelet.
note: Community vote leans this way (62%/38%) though the kubelet coordinates the process.

q: The IPv4/IPv6 dual stack in Kubernetes:
o: Translates an IPv4 request from a service to an IPv6 service.
Allows accessing the IPv4 address using the IPv6 address.
Requires NetworkPolicies to prevent services from mixing requests.
Allows you to create IPv4 and IPv6 dual stack services.
e: Dual-stack lets Pods/Services get both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

q: What does 'continuous' mean in the context of CI/CD?
o: Frequent releases, manual processes, repeatable, fast processing
Periodic releases, manual processes, repeatable, automated processing
Frequent releases, automated processes, repeatable, fast processing
Periodic releases, automated processes, repeatable, automated processing
e: 'Continuous' implies frequent, automated, repeatable, and fast delivery processes.

q: What is ephemeral storage?
o: Storage space that need not persist across restarts.
Storage used by multiple consumers (e.g., multiple Pods).
Storage that is always provisioned locally.
e: Ephemeral storage does not need to survive container/Pod restarts.

q: What is the reference implementation of the OCI runtime specification?
e: runc is the OCI reference implementation for running containers per the runtime-spec.

q: What is a Service?
o: A static network mapping from a Pod to a port.
A way to expose an application running on a set of Pods.
The network configuration for a group of Pods.
An NGINX load balancer deployed for an application.
e: A Service exposes a set of Pods as a network-accessible application.

q: What's the difference between a security profile and a security context?
o: Security Contexts configure Clusters/Namespaces; profiles enforce Security Context settings.
Security Contexts configure Pods/Containers at runtime; profiles are control-plane mechanisms enforcing settings.
Security Profiles configure Pods/Containers; Contexts are control-plane mechanisms.
Security Profiles configure Clusters/Namespaces; Contexts enforce Profile settings.
e: SecurityContext sets Pod/container runtime settings, while security profiles (like Pod Security Standards) enforce policy on those settings.

q: At which layer would distributed tracing be implemented in a cloud native deployment?
e: Distributed tracing instruments application-level request flows.

q: What framework does Kubernetes use to authenticate users with JSON Web Tokens?
e: Kubernetes supports OIDC-based authentication using JWTs.

q: Which feature does Kubernetes provide by default as a container orchestration tool?
e: Deployments provide automated, controlled rollouts and rollbacks by default.

q: Which statement about container runtimes in Kubernetes is true?
o: If iptables sees bridged traffic, you don't need a container runtime.
If you enable IPv4 forwarding, you don't need a container runtime.
Container runtimes are deprecated; install CRI on each node instead.
You must install a container runtime on each node to run pods on it.
e: A container runtime is mandatory on every node to actually run Pod containers.

q: If a Pod was waiting for container images to download on the scheduled node, what state would it be in?
e: A Pod remains Pending while its containers/images are not yet ready to run.

q: What is CloudEvents?
o: A spec for event data formats for K8s network traffic and cloud providers.
A spec for event data formats across all cloud providers only.
A spec for describing event data in common formats for interoperability across services/platforms/systems.
A K8s spec for event data for iCloud/iOS/iMac.
e: CloudEvents is a CNCF spec standardizing event data formats for cross-system interoperability.

q: What is the main purpose of etcd in Kubernetes?
o: etcd stores all cluster data in a key-value store.
etcd stores containers for disaster recovery.
etcd stores copies of config files in /etc/.
etcd stores YAML definitions for all cluster components.
e: etcd is the authoritative key-value store for all cluster state.

q: Releasing open-source software for the first time, which is a valid semantic version?
e: 0.1.0-rc follows the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-prerelease] SemVer format.

q: Which cloud native tools keep clusters in sync with Git and automate updates on new code?
e: Flux and Argo CD are the primary GitOps continuous-delivery tools that sync clusters to Git.

q: Which tool is used to streamline installing and managing Kubernetes applications?
e: Helm is the Kubernetes package manager for installing/managing apps via charts.

q: What are the two steps performed by the kube-scheduler to select a node to schedule a pod?
e: The scheduler filters out infeasible nodes, then scores the rest to pick the best one.

q: Which tool is commonly used alongside Prometheus for data visualization?
e: Grafana is the standard dashboarding tool paired with Prometheus.

q: Which item is a Kubernetes node component?
e: kube-proxy runs on every node; scheduler/etcd are control-plane, kubectl is a client tool.

q: In a serverless computing architecture:
o: Users are charged based on the number of requests to a function.
Serverless functions are incompatible with containerized functions.
Users must reserve capacity based on usage estimates.
Containers serving requests run in the background idle.
e: Serverless billing is typically usage/request-based, not reservation-based.

q: How is application data maintained in containers?
e: Persistent application data is stored in volumes attached to the Pod/container.

q: Which scenario would benefit the most from a service mesh architecture?
o: A few apps with hundreds of pod replicas across multiple clusters.
Thousands of distributed apps in a single cluster.
Tens of distributed apps across multiple clusters.
Thousands of distributed apps across multiple clusters, each providing multiple services.
e: Service meshes shine most at the largest, most complex, multi-cluster microservice topologies.

q: Kubernetes ___ protect you against voluntary interruptions (e.g., deleting Pods, draining nodes).
e: PodDisruptionBudgets limit how many Pods can be voluntarily disrupted at once.

q: What sentence is true about CronJobs in Kubernetes?
o: A CronJob creates one or multiple Jobs on a repeating schedule.
A CronJob creates one container on a repeating schedule.
CronJobs are useful on Linux but obsolete in Kubernetes.
The CronJob schedule format differs from Linux cron.
e: A CronJob creates Job objects according to a cron-style repeating schedule.

q: What is the purpose of the kube-proxy?
o: It balances network requests to pods.
It maintains network rules on nodes.
It ensures cluster connectivity to the internet.
It maintains the DNS rules of the cluster.
e: kube-proxy maintains per-node network rules that implement Service routing.

q: Manual reclamation policy of a PVC resource is known as:
e: The Retain reclaim policy requires manual cleanup/reclamation of the underlying volume.

q: Which component of the Kubernetes architecture integrates with the CRI container runtime?
e: The kubelet talks to the container runtime via the CRI.

q: Which is an open source runtime security tool?
e: Falco is a CNCF runtime security/threat-detection tool.

q: What are the advantages of adopting a GitOps approach for deployments?
o: Reduce failed deployments, operational costs, and fragile release processes.
Reduce failed deployments, configuration drift, and fragile release processes.
Reduce failed deployments, operational costs, and learn git.
Reduce failed deployments, configuration drift, and improve reputation.
e: GitOps reduces failed deployments, configuration drift, and fragile manual release processes.

q: Which command lists the running containers (pods) in the current Kubernetes namespace?
e: kubectl get pods lists Pods in the current namespace.

q: Which is a good habit for cloud native cost efficiency?
o: Follow an automated approach to cost optimization, with visibility and forecasting.
Follow manual processes for cost analysis.
Use only one cloud provider to simplify analysis.
Keep legacy workloads unchanged to avoid cloud costs.
e: Automated cost visibility and forecasting is the recommended FinOps practice.

q: Which of these is a valid container restart policy?
e: Valid restart policies are Always, OnFailure, and Never.

q: Which is a challenge derived from running cloud native applications?
o: Operational costs of maintaining a company data center.
Cost optimization is complex across different public cloud environments.
Lack of container images available in public repositories.
Lack of services provided by common public clouds.
e: Managing and optimizing cost across multiple cloud environments is a well-known cloud native challenge.

q: What is the correct hierarchy of Kubernetes components?
e: The nesting order is Cluster contains Nodes, which host Pods, which contain Containers.

q: Which statement about Secrets is correct?
o: A Secret is part of a Pod specification.
Secrets data is encrypted with the cluster private key by default.
Secrets data is base64 encoded and stored unencrypted by default.
A Secret can only be used for confidential data.
e: By default, Secret values are only base64-encoded in etcd, not encrypted.

q: Which mechanism allows extending the Kubernetes API?
e: CRDs are the primary mechanism for adding new custom API types.

q: Which observability data stream is most useful for plotting resource consumption and predicted future exhaustion?
e: Metrics are numeric time-series data ideal for plotting trends and forecasting.
note: Some community sources favor Logs (C), but Metrics is the technically correct choice for plotting consumption over time.

q: What can be used to create a job that runs at specified times/dates or on a repeating schedule?
e: CronJob is the resource for scheduled/repeating job execution.

q: If kubectl is failing to retrieve information from the cluster, where can you find pod logs to troubleshoot?
e: Pod logs are stored on the node filesystem under /var/log/pods/.

q: Which component watches for newly created Pods with no assigned node, and selects a node for them?
e: The kube-scheduler assigns unscheduled Pods to nodes.

q: Which control plane component updates the node Ready condition if a node becomes unreachable?
e: The node controller (part of kube-controller-manager) marks nodes NotReady/Unknown when unreachable.

q: Which GitOps engine can be used to orchestrate parallel jobs on Kubernetes?
e: Argo Workflows is designed to orchestrate parallel and DAG-based jobs on Kubernetes.
note: Some community answers cite Jenkins X, but Argo Workflows is the engine built specifically for parallel job orchestration.

q: What is the main purpose of the Open Container Initiative (OCI)?
o: Accelerating adoption of containers and Kubernetes.
Creating open industry standards around container formats and runtimes.
Creating standards around container formats for private purposes.
Improving security of container format standards.
e: OCI's mission is establishing open, vendor-neutral standards for container formats and runtimes.

q: Which are the core features provided by a service mesh?
e: Service meshes provide mTLS-based authentication/authorization along with traffic management and observability.

q: Which options include only mandatory fields to create a Kubernetes object using a YAML file?
e: apiVersion, kind, metadata, and spec are the mandatory top-level fields.

q: Which is the name of a container orchestration software?
e: Apache Mesos is a cluster/container orchestration platform (alongside Kubernetes, Swarm).

q: What happens with a regular pod running in Kubernetes when a node fails?
o: A new pod with the same UID is scheduled to another node after a while.
A new, near-identical pod but with a different UID is scheduled to another node.
By default, a pod can only be scheduled to the same node if it fails.
A new pod is scheduled elsewhere only if configured explicitly.
e: A controller reschedules a replacement Pod (new UID) elsewhere; it isn't the exact same Pod object.

q: What is the minimum number of etcd members required for a highly available Kubernetes cluster?
e: An odd-numbered quorum of at least 3 etcd members is the minimum for HA.

q: What is the main purpose of Ingress in Kubernetes?
o: Access HTTP/HTTPS services by IP address.
Access non-HTTP/HTTPS services by IP address.
Access HTTP/HTTPS services running in the cluster based on their path.
e: Ingress routes external HTTP/HTTPS traffic to in-cluster services based on host/path rules.

q: How can you extend the Kubernetes API?
o: Adding a CustomResourceDefinition or implementing an aggregation layer.
Adding a new version of a resource, e.g., v4beta3.
With the command kubectl extend api as admin.
Adding the desired API object as a kubelet parameter.
e: CRDs and the API aggregation layer are the two supported ways to extend the API.

q: What is an ephemeral container?
o: A specialized container that runs as root for infosec applications.
A specialized container that runs temporarily in an existing Pod.
A specialized container that extends/enhances the 'main' container.
A specialized container that runs before the app container in a Pod.
e: Ephemeral containers are added temporarily to a running Pod, typically for debugging.

q: In a cloud native environment, who is usually responsible for maintaining the workloads running across different platforms?
e: The SRE team typically owns keeping workloads running reliably across platforms.

q: Which Kubernetes-native deployment strategy supports zero-downtime updates of a workload?
e: RollingUpdate incrementally replaces old Pods with new ones, avoiding downtime.

q: What service account does a Pod use in a given namespace when the service account is not specified?
e: Pods use the 'default' ServiceAccount of their namespace unless one is specified.

q: What is a cloud native application?
o: A monolithic app that's been containerized and runs on the cloud.
An app designed to be scalable and take advantage of cloud services.
An app designed to run all its functions in separate containers.
Any app that runs in a cloud provider and uses its services.
e: Cloud native apps are designed for scalability and to leverage the dynamic nature of cloud platforms.

q: What's the most adopted way of conflict resolution and decision-making for CNCF open-source projects?
e: CNCF projects rely on open discussion followed by community voting.

q: Which options include resources cleaned by the Kubernetes garbage collection mechanism?
o: Nodes deleted by a cloud controller manager and obsolete kubelet logs.
Unused containers/images and obsolete kubelet logs.
Terminated pods, completed jobs, and objects without owner references.
e: Kubernetes garbage collection removes terminated pods, completed jobs, and orphaned objects lacking owner references.
note: Some community answers point to option B, but the Kubernetes docs support this answer.

q: What is the default eviction timeout when the Ready condition of a node is Unknown or False?
e: The default node monitor grace period before eviction is five minutes.

q: What is the main purpose of a DaemonSet?
o: A DaemonSet ensures that all (or certain) nodes run a copy of a Pod.
A DaemonSet ensures the kubelet is constantly up and running.
A DaemonSet ensures as many pods run as specified in the replicas field.
A DaemonSet ensures a process (agent) runs on every node.
e: A DaemonSet's job is ensuring a Pod copy runs on all (or a selected subset of) nodes.

q: Why do administrators need a container orchestration tool?
o: To manage the lifecycle of a large number of containers.
To assess security risks of container images in production.
To learn how to transform monoliths into microservices.
Because orchestration tools like Kubernetes are the future.
e: Orchestration tools exist to manage the lifecycle of many containers at scale.

q: Which two elements are shared between containers in the same pod?
e: Containers in a Pod can share storage volumes and always share the network namespace.

q: In Kubernetes, if the API version of a feature is v2beta3, it means that:
o: The version stays available for all future releases of that major version.
The API may change in incompatible ways in a later release without notice.
The software is well tested and enabling it is considered safe.
The software may contain bugs; enabling the feature may expose bugs.
e: Beta APIs can still change in breaking ways before reaching stable, even though the code is reasonably well tested.
note: The community vote leans toward C ('well tested, considered safe'), which matches how the Kubernetes docs describe beta features generally — treat this one as worth double-checking.

q: What is the API that exposes resource metrics from the metrics-server?
e: metrics.k8s.io is the resource-metrics API served by metrics-server.

q: Which resource helps in managing a stateless application workload on a Kubernetes cluster?
e: Deployments are the standard resource for managing stateless workloads.

q: Which mechanism can be used to automatically adjust the amount of resources for an application?
e: VPA adjusts CPU/memory requests/limits (resource amount) of existing Pods, unlike HPA which changes replica count.

q: Which is a recommended security habit in Kubernetes?
o: Run containers as group ID 0 (root) and any user ID.
Disallow privilege escalation from within a container by default.
Run containers as user ID 0 (root) and any group ID.
Allow privilege escalation from within a container by default.
e: Disabling privilege escalation by default is a core Pod security best practice.

q: What are the 3 pillars of Observability?
e: Metrics, Logs, and Traces are the classic three pillars of observability.

q: What edge and service proxy tool is designed to be integrated with cloud native applications?
e: Envoy is the widely used edge/service proxy at the heart of many service meshes.

q: What is Flux constructed with?
e: Flux is built on the GitOps Toolkit components.

q: In Kubernetes, which abstraction defines a logical set of Pods and a policy by which to access them?
e: This is the definition of a Kubernetes Service.

q: What does the livenessProbe in Kubernetes help detect?
o: When a container has started successfully.
When a container is ready to serve traffic.
When a container exceeds resource limits.
e: A livenessProbe checks whether a container is still healthy/responsive, restarting it if not.

q: Which command updates the image of a running deployment without recreating the resource?
o: kubectl set image deployment/my-app rollout restart
e: kubectl set image updates a container's image in-place, triggering a rolling update.

q: An admin needs Pods in the test namespace to enforce the Restricted Pod Security Standard. What action should be taken?
o: Apply a PodSecurityAdmission configuration with the Restricted standard to the namespace.
Update RoleBindings to limit access to specific users.
Set a PodSecurityStandard annotation on each Pod.
Create a NetworkPolicy restricting access to Pods.
e: Pod Security Admission is configured at the namespace level via labels to enforce a standard like Restricted.

q: Kubernetes Secrets hold confidential data. Which API object should hold non-confidential data?
e: ConfigMaps are meant for non-sensitive configuration data.

q: When a Kubernetes Secret is created, how is the data stored by default in etcd?
o: As Base64-encoded strings with no actual encryption.
As plain text values with no encoding.
As encrypted records protected by a control-plane master key.
e: By default Secret data is only base64-encoded in etcd, not encrypted.

q: Which cloud native proxy is used for ingress/egress in a service mesh and can also serve as an application gateway?
e: Envoy is commonly used both as a mesh sidecar and as an edge/ingress gateway.

q: Which command retrieves container logs from a specific container in a multi-container Pod?
e: The -c flag on kubectl logs selects which container's logs to show in a multi-container Pod.

q: Which is a primary use case of Istio in a Kubernetes cluster?
o: Service mesh capabilities: traffic management, observability, and security between services.
Secure built-in database management for application workloads.
Managing container runtime versions between services.
Provisioning and managing persistent storage volumes.
e: Istio is a service mesh providing traffic management, observability, and security.

q: Which option represents Pod Security Standards ordered from most permissive to most restrictive?
e: The order from most permissive to most restrictive is Privileged, Baseline, Restricted.

q: What is an advantage of using the Gateway API compared to Ingress in Kubernetes?
o: Clearer role separation between infrastructure providers and application developers.
Exposing an application externally with just a Service resource.
Configuring routing rules through annotations on Ingress resources.
Automatically scaling workloads based on CPU/memory.
e: Gateway API's role-oriented resource model separates infra and app-developer concerns more cleanly than Ingress annotations.

q: An app runs in a logical chain: Gateway API, Service, EndpointSlice, and Container. What object is missing?
e: A Pod sits between EndpointSlice and Container in that chain — EndpointSlices point to Pod IPs, and Pods hold Containers.

q: Which kubectl patch command correctly updates a container's image in a Deployment without recreating it?
e: The patch must target the full path spec.template.spec.containers to reach the Pod template's container list.

q: Which Kubernetes Service type exposes a service only within the cluster?
e: ClusterIP is the default type, reachable only from inside the cluster.

q: What is the main role of CoreDNS within a cluster?
o: Provides consistent DNS names for Pods/Services that need to communicate.
Converts IPv6 calls to IPv4 for dual-stack Pods.
Acts as a DNS server for VMs outside the cluster.
Provides DNS as a Service for user-owned domains.
e: CoreDNS is the cluster's internal DNS server, resolving Pod/Service names.

q: A Pod's kubectl get pods shows READY 0/1. What feature causes this?
e: A failing readiness probe keeps the container marked not-ready, showing 0/1.

q: An app needs to securely access the Kubernetes API without a developer's personal credentials. What's correct?
o: Create a ServiceAccount and bind it to the Pod for API access.
Generate a certificate for the application to access the API.
Use the default ServiceAccount in the namespace.
Use a developer's kubeconfig file with restricted permissions.
e: A dedicated ServiceAccount bound to the Pod is the standard, secure way to grant API access.

q: What are the two essential operations that the kube-scheduler normally performs?
e: Filtering (feasible nodes) and Scoring (best node) are the scheduler's two core steps.

q: Which set of resources can receive automatic updates from the HorizontalPodAutoscaler?
e: HPA can target Deployments and StatefulSets (scalable resources with a replicas field), not DaemonSets or bare Pods.

q: Which option represents best practices when building container images?
o: Multi-stage builds, pin base image to a digest, only install necessary packages.
Multi-stage builds, pin to a digest, install extra packages just in case.
Avoid multi-stage builds, use 'latest' tag, install extra packages.
Multi-stage builds, use 'latest' tag, only install necessary packages.
e: Best practice combines multi-stage builds, pinned digests, and minimal installed packages.

q: Which open source cloud native storage orchestrator automates deployment/management of Ceph for self-managing, self-scaling, self-healing storage?
e: Rook is the CNCF storage orchestrator that automates Ceph (and other backends) on Kubernetes.

q: In Kubernetes, what is the primary responsibility of the kubelet running on each worker node?
o: Providing internal DNS resolution and routing Service traffic.
Allocating persistent storage volumes and managing data replication.
Ensuring containers defined in Pod specs are running and remain healthy on the node.
Managing cluster state and all scheduling decisions.
e: The kubelet's core job is keeping the containers of assigned Pods running and healthy.

q: What is the role of the ingressClassName field in a Kubernetes Ingress resource?
o: Indicates which Ingress Controller should implement the rules.
Specifies the backend Service used by the controller.
Defines the protocol (HTTP/HTTPS) the controller should process.
Determines routing-rule priority across multiple Ingress objects.
e: ingressClassName selects which Ingress Controller implementation should handle that Ingress.

q: What does SBOM stand for?
o: Security Baseline for Open Source Management
e: SBOM = Software Bill of Materials, listing a software's components/dependencies.

q: Which Helm command deletes the release mysql-1234 from the Kubernetes cluster?
e: helm uninstall removes a release and its resources from the cluster.

q: Which statement accurately reflects principles of collaborative development and community stewardship?
o: Community events and working groups foster collaboration and knowledge sharing.
Maintainers act independently without contributor input.
Community stewardship guides growth but excludes sustainability.
Open source succeeds when contributors skip community engagement.
e: Open source communities thrive through events, working groups, and shared knowledge, not isolated decision-making.

q: What is the goal of load balancing?
o: Reschedule application instances across nodes for efficiency.
Distribute traffic between different application versions as a deployment strategy.
Distribute requests evenly across instances to improve availability/reliability.
Measure and compare request performance across instances.
e: Load balancing evenly spreads requests to improve availability and reliability.

q: What happens if only a limit is specified for a resource and no admission-time default request applies?
o: Kubernetes copies the specified limit and uses it as the requested value.
Kubernetes creates the container but it fails with CrashLoopBackOff.
Kubernetes chooses a random value as the requested value.
Kubernetes disallows container creation without request values.
e: If only a limit is set with no default request, Kubernetes sets the request equal to the limit.

q: Which action is supported when working with Pods in Kubernetes?
o: Creating Pods through workload resources like Deployments.
Guaranteeing Pods always stay on the same node once scheduled.
Managing static Pods directly through the API server.
Renaming containers in a Pod using kubectl patch.
e: Pods are normally created indirectly through higher-level controllers like Deployments.

q: In Kubernetes, what is the primary purpose of using annotations?
o: Specify the deployment strategy for applications.
Control access permissions for users and service accounts.
Provide a way to attach metadata to objects.
Define specifications for resource limits and requests.
e: Annotations attach arbitrary, non-identifying metadata to objects.

q: A Pod named my-app must run a simple nginx container. Which kubectl command should be used?
e: kubectl run <name> --image=<image> is the imperative command to create a single Pod.

q: What is the correct method to forward a local port to a specific port inside a Pod?
e: kubectl port-forward tunnels a local port directly to a Pod's port.

q: A Pod is returning a CrashLoopBackOff status. What is the most likely reason?
o: The container's image is missing or cannot be pulled.
There are insufficient resources allocated for the Pod.
The Pod cannot communicate with the API server.
The application inside the container crashed after starting.
e: CrashLoopBackOff specifically indicates the container starts, then repeatedly crashes.

q: An SRE needs to temporarily prevent new Pods from being scheduled on node-2, keeping existing workloads running. Which command?
e: kubectl cordon marks a node unschedulable for new Pods while leaving existing Pods running.

q: In Kubernetes, what is the primary purpose of creating a Service resource for a Deployment?
o: Automatically adjust Pod count based on utilization.
Provide a stable endpoint for accessing Pods even as IPs change.
Define and attach persistent volumes for data across restarts.
e: A Service gives a stable network identity independent of the churn of individual Pod IPs.

q: Which statement best describes the role of kubelet on a Kubernetes worker node?
o: kubelet monitors cluster-wide resource usage and assigns Pods to nodes.
kubelet is the primary API component storing cluster state.
kubelet manages the container runtime and ensures scheduled Pods run as expected.
kubelet configures networking rules for Service traffic routing.
e: The kubelet works with the container runtime to keep scheduled Pods running correctly.

q: What is the primary purpose of a Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) in Kubernetes?
o: Allocate and manage persistent volumes for stateful apps.
Track performance metrics and report node/Pod health.
Automatically scale the number of Pod replicas based on resource utilization.
Coordinate rolling updates when deploying new versions.
e: HPA automatically adjusts replica count based on observed resource utilization.

q: A request for 500 mebibytes of ephemeral storage must be specified in YAML. How should this be written?
e: Mebibytes are expressed with the 'Mi' suffix (binary units), so 500Mi is correct.

q: What command is often used to troubleshoot a failing Pod?
e: kubectl describe surfaces events and status details useful for troubleshooting.

q: Which scenario best illustrates the use case for a StatefulSet?
o: A web app needing multiple replicas for load balancing.
A service routing traffic to various microservices.
A database requiring persistent storage and stable network identities.
A background job that runs periodically without state.
e: StatefulSets are designed for apps like databases needing stable identity and persistent storage per replica.

q: Which file in a Helm chart defines the default configuration values that can be overridden during deployment?
e: values.yaml holds the default configurable values for a chart's templates.

q: Which command is the most efficient way to check the progress of a Deployment rollout and confirm success?
e: kubectl rollout status is purpose-built to report live rollout progress and completion.

q: In a Kubernetes cluster, what is the primary role of the Kubernetes scheduler?
o: Manage the lifecycle of Pods by restarting them when they fail.
Monitor the health of nodes and pods in the cluster.
Handle network traffic between services within the cluster.
Distribute Pods across nodes based on resource availability and constraints.
e: The scheduler assigns Pods to nodes based on resource availability, constraints, and policies.

q: An admin wants to limit total memory usage of all Pods in a namespace to 4Gi. What should they create?
e: A ResourceQuota caps aggregate resource consumption (like total memory) within a namespace.

q: How does cert-manager integrate with Kubernetes resources to provide TLS certificates for an application?
o: It injects TLS certificates directly into Pods at deploy time.
It manages Certificate resources and Secrets that Ingress objects can use for TLS.
It updates kube-proxy config to encrypt traffic between Services.
It replaces default Kubernetes API certificates with external ones.
e: cert-manager issues and manages Certificate custom resources, storing results as Secrets used by Ingress for TLS.

q: In Kubernetes, what is the primary function of a RoleBinding?
o: Create and define a new Role object with specific permissions.
Enforce namespace network rules by binding policies to Pods.
Assign the permissions of a Role to a user, group, or service account within a namespace.
Provide a user/group with cluster-wide permissions across all resources.
e: A RoleBinding grants the permissions of a Role to specific subjects within a namespace.

q: A Pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff. What is the correct way to troubleshoot this?
o: Use kubectl top pod and scale the Deployment to more replicas.
Use kubectl describe pod to review events, then kubectl logs to inspect output.
Use kubectl get nodes and kubectl apply -f to restart the Pod.
Use kubectl exec -- bash and check /var/log/kubelet.log.
e: describe reveals recent events, and logs shows the actual crash output — the standard troubleshooting flow.

q: What is the Kubernetes abstraction that allows groups of Pods to be exposed inside a Kubernetes cluster?
e: A Service exposes a logical grouping of Pods within (or outside) the cluster.

q: What is an important consideration when choosing a base image for a container in a Kubernetes deployment?
o: It should be the largest available image to include all dependencies.
It should always be the latest version for newest features.
It should be minimal and purpose-built to reduce attack surface and improve performance.
It can be any existing public image without considering its contents.
e: Minimal, purpose-built base images reduce attack surface and improve build/runtime efficiency.

q: When modifying an existing Helm release to apply new configuration values, which approach is best practice?
o: Edit the chart source files directly and reapply them.
Use kubectl edit to modify the live release resources.
Delete the release and reinstall it with the desired configuration.
Use helm upgrade with --set to apply new values while preserving release history.
e: helm upgrade --set applies new values in a tracked, reversible way, preserving release history.

q: Which field in a Pod or Deployment manifest ensures that Pods are scheduled only on nodes with specific labels?
e: nodeSelector matches Pods to nodes carrying the specified label.

q: What is the purpose of the Gateway API in Kubernetes?
o: Collect, monitor, and log performance metrics for applications.
Define and manage persistent storage resources used by Pods.
Provide a standardized interface for managing traffic routing to Services.
Enable apps to automatically scale based on demand.
e: The Gateway API standardizes traffic routing configuration for Services, succeeding Ingress.

q: Why are ServiceAccounts used in Kubernetes when assigning RBAC permissions to Pods?
o: To authenticate Pods via special admin user identities.
To securely store application credentials inside Pods.
To automatically assign Pods cluster-admin permissions.
To let Pods authenticate to the API server securely without personal user credentials.
e: ServiceAccounts give Pods their own identity to authenticate to the API server, avoiding use of personal credentials.

q: In a cloud native environment, how do containerization and virtualization differ in terms of resource management?
o: Containerization consumes more memory than virtualization by default.
Containerization shares the host OS, while virtualization runs a full OS per instance.
Containerization uses hypervisors to manage resources, virtualization does not.
Containerization allocates resources per container, virtualization does not isolate them.
e: Containers share the host kernel/OS, while VMs each run a full guest OS via a hypervisor.

q: Which command could an admin use to prevent Pod scheduling on a node temporarily, for maintenance?
e: kubectl cordon marks the node unschedulable without disturbing existing Pods.

q: A platform engineer wants a new microservice automatically deployed to every cluster registered in Argo CD. Which configuration best achieves this?
o: Create an Argo CD ApplicationSet using a Git repository containing the microservice manifests.
Set up a CronJob that redeploys the microservice on a schedule.
Use a Helm chart with a single Application defined in Argo CD.
Manually configure every registered cluster with the deployment YAML.
e: ApplicationSet is specifically designed to template and deploy an app across many registered clusters automatically.

q: Lightweight network proxies such as Envoy are part of which plane in a service mesh?
e: Sidecar proxies like Envoy form the data plane, handling actual traffic.

q: Which common practice is an antipattern when the GitOps workflow goes live?
o: Deploying Kubernetes objects via imperative commands.
Leaving manual comments in PR discussions.
Deploying Kubernetes objects via declarative manifests.
Pushing builds with the deploy label.
e: Imperative, manual kubectl changes bypass and drift from the Git-declared desired state, defeating GitOps.

q: What command would be used to check the revisions of Deployment web-app?
e: kubectl rollout history lists past revisions of a Deployment.

q: Which statement is true about the Container Storage Interface (CSI) in Kubernetes?
o: CSI is a Kubernetes-only API with in-tree compiled drivers selected via a PersistentVolume.
CSI lets apps mount storage by referencing the driver name directly in the Pod spec.
CSI focuses only on NFS/iSCSI backends with basic volume provisioning.
CSI is a cross-platform spec; in Kubernetes, CSI drivers run as pods with sidecars, consumed via StorageClass/PVC.
e: CSI is portable across orchestrators; in Kubernetes it's implemented as driver pods, used through StorageClass and PVC objects.

q: A deployment must run only on nodes with specific hardware capabilities. What configuration ensures this?
o: Set a PodDisruptionBudget for the deployment.
Use a nodeSelector in the deployment specification.
e: A nodeSelector restricts scheduling to nodes matching a specific label (e.g., hardware type).

q: Which cloud native tool(s) keep clusters in sync with Git config sources and automate updates on new code?
e: Flux and Argo CD are the standard GitOps continuous-delivery tools for this purpose.

q: A Pod shows ErrImagePull status. What is most likely the cause?
o: Kubelet is not running properly on the node.
Kube-scheduler cannot find a node to execute the Pod.
The container image cannot be downloaded.
The container image needs to run using hostNetwork.
e: ErrImagePull specifically indicates the container image could not be pulled/downloaded.

q: Which statement best describes observability in a cloud native environment?
o: Collecting and analyzing logs, metrics, and traces to understand system behavior.
Using alerts and dashboards to notify admins about outages.
Restarting failed Pods to maintain application availability.
Configuring health probes to check container health.
e: Observability broadly means gathering and analyzing telemetry (logs/metrics/traces) to understand system behavior.

q: Which statement best explains the Container Storage Interface (CSI) concept in Kubernetes?
o: CSI is a standard API letting Kubernetes (and other orchestrators) use different storage systems via plugins.
CSI manages container-to-container communication across nodes.
CSI is a Kubernetes-only API providing built-in storage drivers.
CSI is a framework that provisions local node storage without external plugins.
e: CSI is a vendor-neutral standard specification for pluggable storage integration across orchestrators.

q: Gateway API is a successor to what Kubernetes API?
e: Gateway API is designed as the next-generation successor to Ingress.

q: How are ConfigMaps correctly used in Kubernetes applications?
o: To adjust cluster scheduling rules applied by the scheduler.
To keep encrypted secrets such as passwords or tokens.
To provide configuration values that Pods consume as files or variables.
To hold shared log files that applications produce.
e: ConfigMaps supply non-sensitive configuration data to Pods via env vars or mounted files.

q: How is an Argo CD ApplicationSet configured to ensure continuous deployment of an application?
o: Manually deploy via kubectl every time changes are made.
Define the ApplicationSet in YAML and link it to a Git repository containing manifests.
Define an ApplicationSet with deployment parameters and apply via kubectl.
Use a Helm chart packaged and deployed directly, bypassing GitOps.
e: ApplicationSet uses a generator pointing at a Git repo to continuously drive deployments.

q: DNS issues are suspected inside a Pod. Which command is most useful to verify the problem?
o: kubectl delete pod to recreate and test if the issue resolves.
kubectl get endpoints to confirm backend addresses.
kubectl logs to review app output for DNS errors.
kubectl exec -- nslookup to check name resolution directly inside the Pod.
e: Running nslookup from inside the Pod directly tests its DNS resolution against CoreDNS.

q: In Kubernetes RBAC, what is the primary difference between a Role and a ClusterRole?
o: Role is weaker in scope/power; ClusterRole is always stronger.
A Role is namespace-scoped; a ClusterRole is cluster-scoped, applying across all namespaces.
Role defines modify permissions; ClusterRole defines only view permissions.
Role is limited to Pods/Services; ClusterRole can grant access to any resource type.
e: Roles apply within one namespace; ClusterRoles can apply cluster-wide (or be bound within a namespace too).

q: Which Kubernetes resource provides standardized load balancing, TLS termination, and multi-context traffic routing across different implementations?
e: The Gateway API standardizes advanced traffic routing/LB/TLS features across implementations.

q: Which statement describes the purpose of Labels in Kubernetes?
o: Labels must be defined on objects before they can be created.
Labels assign objects to specific namespaces for isolation.
Labels provide globally unique identifiers for all objects.
Labels attach identifying metadata to objects so they can be selected and grouped.
e: Labels are key/value metadata used for selecting and organizing objects.

q: In a Kubernetes cluster, the component called etcd plays an essential role. What is its primary function?
o: Replicate cluster state data across control plane nodes for HA.
Provide a distributed key-value store for all cluster state and data.
Persist API object definitions such as Pods, ConfigMaps, Secrets.
Maintain desired state of workloads by reconciling changes through controllers.
e: etcd's core role is serving as the distributed key-value store holding all cluster state.

q: What is the correct command to scale multiple Pods for a deployment?
e: kubectl scale --replicas=<n> sets the desired replica count for a Deployment.

q: Which Pod Security Standard balances ease of adoption while still preventing known privilege escalations?
e: Baseline blocks known privilege-escalation vectors while remaining easy to adopt broadly.

q: A logging agent must be deployed to run on every node in a Kubernetes cluster. Which resource should be used?
e: A DaemonSet automatically runs a Pod copy on every (or selected) node — ideal for logging agents.

q: How can a tls-type secret be created holding a TLS cert and key using kubectl?
e: kubectl create secret tls uses --cert and --key flags specifically for the TLS secret type.

q: In a Kubernetes cluster, how does DNS resolution work for services?
o: Uses the IP addresses of the Pods directly.
Handled by an external DNS provider managing all service names.
Kubernetes creates service names that resolve to stable cluster IPs.
Service names are resolved using environment variables set in each Pod.
e: Cluster DNS resolves service names to stable ClusterIPs (or Pod IPs for headless Services).

q: What best describes containerization?
o: A technique for running apps only on bare metal without abstraction.
A lightweight approach to running apps in isolated environments using shared OS resources.
A way to create and manage virtual machines.
A method of virtualizing hardware to run multiple OSes.
e: Containerization isolates applications while sharing the host OS kernel, unlike full virtualization.

q: In a Kubernetes cluster, how are Labels and Selectors utilized to manage and organize resources?
o: Labels are used only for service discovery.
Labels categorize resources; Selectors filter and retrieve resources based on those labels.
Selectors can only be applied to Pods.
Labels are auto-generated; Selectors are manually defined.
e: Labels tag resources with metadata, and Selectors query/filter resources by that metadata.

q: What is the primary role of a Service in a Kubernetes cluster?
o: It exposes an application running behind a single outward-facing endpoint.
To store configuration data and secrets in the cluster.
To provide internet access into the cluster.
To manage automatic scaling of applications.
e: A Service provides one stable endpoint for a set of backing Pods.

q: What happens if a container runtime is missing on Kubernetes worker nodes?
o: Nodes cannot communicate with each other.
Pods cannot communicate with each other.
e: Without a container runtime, the kubelet has no way to actually start containers for Pods.

q: Which Pod Security Standard enforces the most restrictive settings, designed for security-critical workloads?
e: Restricted is the most locked-down of the three official Pod Security Standards.

q: Which statement is correct about Role and ClusterRole objects in Kubernetes?
o: Roles can only set permissions for resources within a particular namespace.
ClusterRoles and Roles can remove permissions from resources within a namespace.
ClusterRoles can only set permissions for non-namespaced resources.
Roles can set permissions for both namespaced and non-namespaced objects.
e: A Role's permissions are always scoped to a single namespace.

q: What are the possible options for PolicyTypes when configuring a NetworkPolicy?
e: NetworkPolicy PolicyTypes are Ingress and Egress.

q: A Pod needs to be configured for a slow-starting application, only marked ready once fully initialized. What's the best approach?
o: Use both liveness and startup probes.
Use both readiness and startup probes.
e: A startup probe delays liveness/readiness checks; combined with a readiness probe, the Pod is only marked ready once initialized.

q: A node is scheduled for maintenance. How can Pods on that node be identified so workloads can be redirected first?
e: Listing all Pods with -o wide (filtered by node) shows which Pods are running where.

q: By default Pods are non-isolated. When a NetworkPolicy selects a Pod, it becomes isolated. How are multiple NetworkPolicies on the same Pod handled?
e: Multiple NetworkPolicies applied to the same Pod are combined additively (union of allowed traffic).

q: CNCF organizes different Kubernetes related events: meetups, KubeCons, KubeDays, KCDs, etc. What does KCD stand for?
e: KCD = Kubernetes Community Days.

q: Which command correctly uses kubectl exec to inspect environment variables inside a running container?
e: kubectl exec <pod> -- env runs the env command inside the container.

q: A node worker-1 needs maintenance; workloads must be safely evicted and rescheduled. Which command?
e: kubectl drain safely evicts Pods from a node (ignoring DaemonSets) before maintenance.

q: Which CNCF project is primarily used as a high-performance proxy for microservices, handling service-to-service communication, load balancing, and observability in service meshes?
e: Envoy is the CNCF proxy widely used as the data-plane component of service meshes.

q: Which Kubernetes feature is the simplest way to force a Pod or Deployment to run only on nodes with a specific label?
e: nodeSelector is the simplest label-based scheduling constraint, simpler than full node affinity.

q: What is the primary purpose of an Ingress resource in Kubernetes?
o: Monitor the health status of application Pods.
Expose internal services to external web traffic.
Store configuration data used by applications.
Manage persistent volumes for application data.
e: Ingress exposes internal Services to external HTTP/HTTPS traffic.

q: In Kubernetes, how do Namespaces differ from Labels in managing resources within a cluster?
o: Namespaces can only contain Pods, but Labels apply to any resource.
Namespaces are static, while Labels can be modified dynamically.
Namespaces are only for access control; Labels are solely for monitoring.
Namespaces isolate resources, while Labels are used for query and selection.
e: Namespaces partition/isolate resources; Labels are metadata used to query and select across resources.

q: A team's ML workload performs best on nodes labeled disk=ssd but must still run elsewhere if none are available. Which scheduling rule?
e: 'Preferred' node affinity expresses a soft preference, falling back to other nodes if unmet.

q: What is the main role of CNCF Ambassadors in the cloud native ecosystem?
o: Promote cloud native adoption by supporting communities, organizing events, and advocating for CNCF projects.
Handle CNCF operations: budgets, sponsors, agreements.
Design Kubernetes features: writing code, planning releases.
Manage project governance: guiding development, reviewing code.
e: CNCF Ambassadors are community advocates who promote adoption and organize local events.

q: Prometheus has 4 core metric types: Summary, Histogram, Gauge. What is the 4th metric type?
e: The four core Prometheus metric types are Counter, Gauge, Histogram, and Summary.

q: How can a Pod be configured to use a ServiceAccount for authenticated API access?
o: Attach the ServiceAccount directly to the kube-scheduler.
Specify the ServiceAccount name in the Pod spec; Kubernetes mounts its token as a volume.
Embed the ServiceAccount token inside the container image at build time.
Convert the ServiceAccount into a ConfigMap consumed as environment variables.
